title: The Kangaroo step and the Tacky Annie
summary: Green lists new songs, demonstrates Chuckles' Kangaroo step from George White's New Shuffle Along and compares it with the Tacky Annie.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So tell me some of the -- can you tell me some of the routines that you used to do, some of the joking you used to do, and maybe even some of the dancing at this point?

Yeah, well, it mostly consisted of introducing new songs, like, 'Scatting at the Kit Kat,' 'Born to Swing,' and 'Kangaroo,' that was the new dance, but it was mostly visual. There was an off-Broadway show, we introduced that song about the kangaroo, and Chuckles invented, created, a step. It was just one step. It wasn't a whole dance.
Well, it's only eight bars of music, you see.
I think I'd like to see that one, too.
It's something similar to the Tacky Annie, but you do it I think about four times instead of once, on each side of the body.
Sure. I'll give you a degree.
That is a bit like the Tacky Annie, but not quite as sophisticated.
Can you do the Tacky Annie?

That's the Tacky Annie, yes. That was the Tacky Annie. The Tacky Annie, of course, you use both feet equally, and I see with the Kangaroo you were doing something more on one foot more than the other. Would you agree with that?

As I say, it's not as sophisticated as the Tacky Annie. The Tacky Annie is really a nice dance step. It looks lovely on girls, I think. It's really a lovely step for girls. I was about an animal, the Kangaroo, and it's that hopping.

(Inaudible). Chuckles, he invented the step. They seemed to like it, you know. We would never do any tap dance routines unless it was agreed for to do by the office, Nat Nazzarro, or Bubbles, either one, you see. At that time, see. But that was in a show for Mr. White, you know, George White, the George White Scandals. Well, he introduced this other show he called -- I think it was the New Shuffle Along of 1930 -- something -- '37 or '8, somewhere in there.
It was about 30 something, -- Shuffle Along.

Yes. The New Shuffle Along was based on some visitors to Africa, and they was deep in the jungles and they had costumes made up of different animals, these visitors. They would have these costumes made like they was some other animal, in case they -- to avoid danger, see. But the thing about it is Africa wasn't Australia, and that's where the Kangaroo was. But it was mostly -- it was about comedy. It was happy times, you know. It was during the Depression, and they was getting over the Depression at that time, and --
